definition: Distinguishing subjective language (opinions, evaluations) from objective statements in text.
details: Distinguishing subjective language (opinions, evaluations) from objective statements in text. It serves as a preprocessing step for sentiment analysis and opinion mining.

explainer.lead: Subjectivity analysis distinguishes subjective language (opinions, evaluations) from objective statements in text. It matters as a preprocessing step for sentiment analysis and opinion mining.

tiers.eli5: It is how a program sorts a sentence into 'this is a fact' versus 'this is what someone thinks'.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers run it before sentiment analysis so opinions are separated from factual statements. A pitfall is that mixing the two upstream muddies downstream sentiment results.
tiers.paperLevel: Distinguishing subjective language (opinions, evaluations) from objective statements in text; serves as preprocessing for sentiment analysis and opinion mining.

explainer.example: In a product review, the sentence stating a specification is tagged objective while the sentence praising it is tagged subjective.
